item.question: Do these designs have reflection symmetry also? Draw the lines of symmetry.
steps_tex: The two designs are the green and pink square and the square coloured orange and blue.
Green and pink square: fold it along a diagonal, from one corner to the opposite corner. The two halves land on each other, green on green and pink on pink. So each diagonal is a line of symmetry.
Fold it along the vertical line: the green square would land on a pink square. That is not a line of symmetry. The horizontal line does the same.
So the green and pink square has $2$ lines of symmetry, the two diagonals.
Orange and blue square: fold it along any dashed line. Every triangle would land on a triangle of the other colour. So there is no line of symmetry.
This design looks the same after a turn, but it has no reflection symmetry.

concept_name: A Half Print and Its Line of Symmetry

item.question: A block is carved in the shape of a leaf with a stem down the middle. Its half print shows only the left half of the leaf. What does the whole print look like?
steps: The half print has one straight edge. That edge is the line of symmetry.
The straight edge runs down the middle of the leaf, along the stem.
Draw the same half on the other side of the line, as if the paper were folded along the edge.
The two halves together make the whole leaf.
Check: fold the whole print along the line and the two halves land on each other.
item.answer: The whole print is the half print together with its copy on the other side of the straight edge
item.text:
Worked example: A block is carved in the shape of a leaf with a stem down the middle. Its half print shows only the left half of the leaf. What does the whole print look like?

4. The two halves together make the whole leaf.

Answer: The whole print is the half print together with its copy on the other side of the straight edge

item.question: A flower block is stamped 2 times, with a 1/2 turn between the stamps. Does the print look the same after a 1/2 turn? After a 1/4 turn?
steps: The first stamp puts a flower at the top.
A 1/2 turn of the block puts the second flower at the bottom.
Turn the print a 1/2 turn: the top flower lands at the bottom and the bottom flower lands at the top. The print looks the same.
Turn the print a 1/4 turn: the flowers would land at the sides, where there are none. The print does not look the same.
Check: 2 stamps match after a 1/2 turn only.
item.answer: After a 1/2 turn it looks the same, and after a 1/4 turn it does not

item.question: Observe the shapes given on the border. Which of the shapes have reflection symmetry? Put a tick mark on them. Put a star mark on the shapes that have rotational symmetry.
steps_tex: Test each shape with a fold line (reflection symmetry) and with a turn (rotational symmetry). The shapes are numbered $1$ to $19$ round the border from the top-left corner, going to the right, then down, then to the left, then up.
Shape $1$, three pink triangles touching at their corners: $3$ lines of symmetry, and it looks the same after a $\frac{1}{3}$ turn. Tick and star.
Shape $2$, the green six-pointed star: $6$ lines, and it looks the same after a $\frac{1}{6}$ turn. Tick and star.
Shape $3$, the yellow six-sided shape: it has a vertical line and a horizontal line of symmetry, and it looks the same after a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn. Tick and star.
Shape $4$, three lilac circles joined to the middle, drawn nearly even: $3$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{3}$ turn. Tick and star.
Shape $5$, the green triangle with grey corners: $3$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{3}$ turn. Tick and star.
Shape $6$, the pink rectangle: $2$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn. Tick and star.
Shape $7$, the grey diamond: $2$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn. Tick and star.
Shape $8$, the five-sided shape with equal sides: $5$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{5}$ turn. Tick and star.
Shape $9$, the lilac ring of small triangles, drawn nearly even: $5$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{5}$ turn. Tick and star.
Shape $10$, the seven-sided shape with equal sides: $7$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{7}$ turn. Tick and star.
Shape $11$, the blue shape of four triangles: $4$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{4}$ turn. Tick and star.
Shape $12$, the pink triangle with three teal circles: $3$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{3}$ turn. Tick and star.
Shape $13$, the orange slanted four-sided shape: no line of symmetry, but it looks the same after a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn. Star only.
Shape $14$, the yellow triangle with three small grey triangles: $3$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{3}$ turn. Tick and star.
Shape $15$, the thin pink triangle with a square corner: no line of symmetry and no turn that works. No mark.
Shape $16$, the two maroon triangles touching at their points: $2$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{2}$ turn. Tick and star.
Shape $17$, the circle: every line through the middle is a line of symmetry, and it looks the same after every turn. Tick and star.
Shape $18$, the blue square: $4$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{4}$ turn. Tick and star.
Shape $19$, the purple triangle with three equal sides: $3$ lines, and a $\frac{1}{3}$ turn. Tick and star.
Check: $17$ shapes get a tick mark, all except $13$ and $15$, and $18$ shapes get a star mark, all except $15$. $17 + 2 = 19$ and $18 + 1 = 19$.
item.answer_tex: Tick mark (reflection symmetry): all shapes except $13$ and $15$. Star mark (rotational symmetry): all shapes except $15$.

item.question: Create symmetrical patterns and designs using vegetable blocks. Some are shown below.
steps_tex: Cut a vegetable, such as a potato, to get a flat face, and carve a simple shape on it. A ladyfinger cut across also gives a flower-like face.
Dip the flat face in colour and press it on paper to make a print.
For a design that looks the same after every $\frac{1}{4}$ turn, stamp the block, turn the paper a $\frac{1}{4}$ turn, and stamp again, $4$ times in all.
For a design with a line of symmetry, use a block that has its own line of symmetry and stamp it on the two sides of a line drawn on the paper, the same distance from the line.
Sort your prints: only rotational symmetry, only reflection symmetry, or both.
Sample answer: your patterns may be different. Your answer may differ.
